exercise.name: Push-up (wall)

reference.title: Push-up (wall)
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be read at authoring time, so the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice)

exercise.mechanics: Compound (shoulder horizontal adduction and elbow extension)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in as you lean toward the wall, breathe out as you push away.

prescription.tempo: About 1.6 s in, short pause, 1.1 s out
prescription.load: Body weight (stand further from the wall for more)
prescription.progression: Feet further back, then incline push-ups on a bench, then floor push-ups

cues.text: Stand facing a wall, feet hip width and about an arm's length or more back. Hands on the wall at shoulder height, a little wider than the shoulders, arms straight.
Lean in as one piece, bending the elbows (about 30-45 degrees from the body) until the face is close to the wall. Heels stay down.
Push the wall away back to straight arms.
Body in one line, then the next rep.

mistakes.fix: Squeeze the glutes and keep the body in one line.

mistakes.mistake: Only bending the neck toward the wall
mistakes.fix: The whole body leans; the head stays in line.
Keep them about 30-45 degrees from the body.

mistakes.mistake: Feet too close to the wall
mistakes.fix: Step back until you feel the chest and arms working.

kinematics.norm: Straight to well bent (about 90 degrees or more) near the wall (common coaching standard)
The whole body leans forward from the ankles; the steeper the body, the lower the load on the hands (push-up load falls as the hands go higher: Wurm 2010)
Shoulder height, a little wider than the shoulders (common coaching standard)
Heels down; the ankles bend as the body leans (clinical opinion)
About 1.6 s in, 1.1 s out (clinical opinion)

sources.title: Wurm, VanderZanden, Spadavecchia, Durocher, Bickham, Petushek and Ebben, kinetic analysis of several variations of push-ups (ISBS 2010 conference proceedings; peak hand force 64% of body mass for a regular push-up, 70% and 74% with the feet on 30.5 cm and 61 cm boxes)
Kim, Kim and Ha 2016, effect of the push-up exercise at different palmar width on muscle activities (J Phys Ther Sci 28(2):446-449; PMC4792988)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Wear shoes that do not slip, or stand on a non-slip surface.
modify: Step closer to the wall to make it easier.
Wrist discomfort: hands a little lower or turned slightly out.
regressions: Smaller range (lean in only part way).
progressions: Knee push-up, then the floor push-up.

muscleNotes.pec_r: Main mover: lower and press the body.
muscleNotes.pec_l: Main mover: lower and press the body.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Keeps the shoulder blades flat on the ribs and pushes them forward at the top.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Keeps the shoulder blades flat on the ribs and pushes them forward at the top.
muscleNotes.core: Holds the body in one straight line.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Stop the hips sagging or twisting.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Stop the hips sagging or twisting.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Control the shoulder blades as they move back and forth.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Control the shoulder blades as they move back and forth.
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Squeeze to keep the hips in line.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Squeeze to keep the hips in line.
muscleNotes.calves_r: Keep the heels down and the ankles steady as the body leans.
muscleNotes.calves_l: Keep the heels down and the ankles steady as the body leans.
